name: matrix_H
description: Representative ATen schema copied verbatim: aten::matrix_H(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a). This representative signature is NOT exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns and defines the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and coverage must never be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schema strings (verbatim): aten::matrix_H(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a) ; aten::matrix_H.a(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a). Both registered overloads take exactly one Tensor named self, and the schemas annotate the single Tensor return as aliasing self, so the same representative parameter model applies; the .a overload is reached in pytest through torch.ops.aten.matrix_H.a while the candidate is called through the single public name flag_gems.matrix_H. Semantics derived from the tests: matrix_H returns a zero-copy (conjugate) transpose view that swaps the last two dimensions without reading any element; for complex input the lazy conjugate bit is toggled rather than a conjugate copy materialised, so layout and aliasing are the contract rather than values. Rank-2 tensors are the supported class and rank 0 is a deprecated scalar path, while rank 1 and rank >= 3 raise RuntimeError and non-Tensor inputs raise RuntimeError or TypeError. The result aliases the input storage: writes through the result are visible in the input (write-through), strides, storage offset, is_conj and _is_view flags match the ATen reference, empty, transposed, column-slice, offset-window and expanded layouts are preserved, backward produces an input gradient equal to the ATen reference gradient on the tested shapes and dtypes, and NaN/Inf payloads pass through unchanged. These mutation, aliasing and error behaviors are described for the representative overload only; overload-dependent behavior remains expressed by the original pytest.
